summary.text: A 67-year-old man presented in February 2022 with a one-month history of dysphagia; EGD showed an obstructing neoplasm at 22 cm from the incisors, biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma with PD-L1 CPS ≥1, and CT showed an upper thoracic esophageal mass with enlarged peri-tumoral nodes (cT3N1M0, stage IIIb, ECOG 0). History included hypertension on amlodipine and 30-pack-year smoking.

He received paclitaxel, nedaplatin and camrelizumab with symptomatic improvement and tumor regression; after four cycles repeat EGD and biopsies showed no residual carcinoma (pathological complete response). Maintenance camrelizumab was complicated by hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine; he declined further maintenance therapy and radiotherapy was omitted.
As of August 2025 he had occasional mild dysphagia with solid foods, no recurrence or metastasis on surveillance CT, and disease-free survival exceeding 42 months.

He had no history of hypertension or diabetes, was a non-smoker and non-drinker.

He declined surgery and completed two additional cycles; a June 2023 EGD and biopsies confirmed pathological complete response. He received 13 cycles of maintenance camrelizumab without immune-related adverse events, then treatment was paused with no recurrence (DFS >31 months).

summary.text: A 66-year-old man presented in July 2023 with a two-month history of dysphagia; EGD showed an ulcerated neoplastic lesion at 31–38 cm from the incisors, pathology confirmed squamous cell carcinoma (PD-L1 CPS ≥1), and CT showed a mid-to-lower esophageal mass with multiple enlarged lymph nodes (cT3N1-2M0, stage IIIb, ECOG 1). History included pleuritis, bilateral pleural thickening with calcification, emphysema, type 2 diabetes on metformin and acarbose, 80-pack-year smoking, occasional alcohol use and esophageal cancer in a brother.

He received two cycles of nab-paclitaxel, nedaplatin and camrelizumab with symptomatic improvement and marked tumor regression on CT, declined esophagectomy and received two more cycles; a November 2023 EGD and biopsies confirmed pathological complete response. He developed Grade 2 RCCEP, declined maintenance therapy, and remains disease-free on surveillance (DFS >25 months); radiotherapy was omitted.

summary.text: A 72-year-old man presented in August 2023 with a four-month history of dysphagia; EGD showed an irregular lesion on the left esophageal wall at 18–21 cm from the incisors, biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma (PD-L1 CPS ≥10), and CT showed upper esophageal wall thickening (cT3N0M0, stage IIa, ECOG 1); the discussion describes the tumor as cervical. He had no history of hypertension or diabetes, was a non-smoker and non-drinker.

He received one cycle of nab-paclitaxel, nedaplatin and camrelizumab, then sequential radiotherapy (50.4 Gy) and three more chemoimmunotherapy cycles; follow-up CT and EGD confirmed pathological complete response. Maintenance camrelizumab was followed by Grade 2 RCCEP and a switch to sintilimab for 13 cycles; treatment was paused after clinical complete response.

In March 2025 dysphagia recurred and progressed; biopsy confirmed recurrence (PFS 18 months). One cycle of nab-paclitaxel, nedaplatin and sintilimab was ineffective with CT-confirmed progressive disease; in May 2025 he was switched to fluorouracil, calcium folinate and nedaplatin plus oral anlotinib, had Grade 2–3 nausea and vomiting, declined further chemotherapy, and continues anlotinib monotherapy with overall survival exceeding 24 months.
